headline: Recommended GE Vernova lease change and Airport Improvement Grant to Council, entered executive session on legal matters, and recommended six-month data center moratorium extension.
summary: The committee heard a University of Maine intern presentation on economic development projects, an airport growth report, follow-ups on electric vehicles, heat pumps, and chicken regulations, and discussed a data center moratorium in executive session. It voted to recommend a GE Vernova lease change and an Airport Improvement Grant to full Council, and recommended extending the data center moratorium for six months.
decisions: Recommended the GE Vernova temporary land lease change to full Council for approval.
Approved staff recommendation to accept and appropriate the Airport Improvement Grant payment.
Entered Executive Session to consult with legal counsel under 1 M.R.S.A § 405(6)(E).
Recommended extending the data center moratorium for six months to full Council.

decision_evidence.quote: Councilor Carson moved that the Committee recommend the lease change to full Council for approval. Seconded by Councilor Fish. Roll call vote conducted – all in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Councilor Carson moved staff recommendation to accept and appropriate the Airport Improvement Grant payment. Seconded by Councilor Faloon. Roll call vote conducted – all in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Councilor Carson moved that pursuant to 1 M.R.S.A § 405(6)(E), consultations with legal counsel, the Committee enter Executive Session. Seconded by Councilor Faloon. Roll call vote conducted – all in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.
Councilor Carson moved that the Committee recommends extending the data center moratorium for six months to full Council. Seconded by Councilor Fish. Vote unless doubted, no doubt.

plain_text:
BUSINESS & ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE
Monday, September 9, 2026 @ 5:15 PM
Council Chambers, First Floor of City Hall
MEETING MINUTES
City Councilors Present: Leonard, Faloon, Mallar, Fish, Carson, Hawes, Beck,
Walker, Deane
City Staff Present: Krieg, Hernandez-Smith, Vologina, Collette
Chair Leonard called the meeting to order at 5:45 P.M.
1. Presentation from University of Maine – Orono Students on their 
Assigned Economic Development Projects
Chair Leonard introduced the agenda item.
Economic Development Officer Hernandez-Smith provided an overview of the internship
program and its value to the department. She introduced Economic Development
Specialist Veronika Vologina and the Economic Development Interns Elle Prescott,
Isabella Gaudio, and Ashley Wilson.
Economic Development Specialist Vologina and Economic Development Interns Gaudio
and Wilson presented on their internship projects, including: Bangor Central Kitchen
documents, Foreign Trade Zone 58, Tax Increment Financing and Credit Enhancement
Agreements, and City properties and leases. They reflected on their growth and provided
feedback on Gen Z retention and pipeline development. 
Economic Development Officer Hernandez-Smith introduced the new director of the
University of Maine’s School of Policy and International Relations, J. Alexander Hamilton,
as well as the incoming Economic Development Intern, Anna Wallace. 
Chair Leonard asked the Committee for questions.
Chair Leonard commented on his appreciation of the use of whimsy, as well as the
responsibility to create a path forward for the next generation in the workforce.
Councilor Beck asked about the process for bringing a project from brainstorming stages
to an official document -- Economic Development Officer Hernandez-Smith described an
example of evaluating whether drafted Foreign Trade Zone documents are better suited
for internal training or for public facing information as a component of zone growth. Beck
asked about the process for creating Tax Increment Financing and Credit Enhancement
Agreement “cheat sheets” -- Hernandez-Smith described tasking Economic Development
Intern Wilson with dissecting the policies from an outside perspective with the intention of
transforming what was found challenging into broken-down and readable information.
Beck asked for the use of this document for incoming Councilors.
Councilor Beck asked if the project dashboard is public facing -- Economic Development
Officer Hernandez-Smith discussed that while its intent is to serve as an internal project
management organizer, pieces will be utilized publicly on the City webpage as well as at
Lunch and Learn sessions with Council.
Councilor Beck noted the importance of institutional memory, asking if the onboarding
guide is something that could be implemented in other departments. Economic
Development Officer Hernandez-Smith discussed that the implementation may depend
on the role, but she believes such guides help with efficiency. 
Councilor Beck asked about Gen Z recruitment and retention -- Economic Development
Officer Hernandez-Smith discussed the importance of succession plans and the ability to
allow young people to interact with municipal government. 
Councilor Carson congratulated the interns and noted that he does believe all of their
projects will contribute a lasting difference.
Councilor Fish thanked the interns and appreciated the thought into simplifying forms to
make them easier for both consumers and Councilors.
Councilor Faloon thanked the interns and applauded their presentation skills.
Councilor Carson thanked the Economic Development team for leveraging anchor
institutions.
2. Bangor International Airport Report
Chair Leonard introduced the agenda item.
Airport Director Saavedra discussed growth at the airport, stating that 2025 provided the
busiest year on record. He shared the statistic that three out of every four arriving
passengers rent a car in Bangor. Saavedra discussed that the 2025 and 2026 summer
season trends, along with feedback from airline partners, means the airport can expect
growth to continue. 
Councilor Leonard asked how the upcoming El Nino may impact the upcoming season
projections for the airport and runway – Airport Director Saavedra discussed the airport’s
federally-required winter operations plan.
Councilor Fish expressed that with increasing fuel charges and tariffs, she is surprised
each month still experienced growth compared to last year. She asked what may be
causing the uptick in tourism. Airport Director Saavedra discussed that although
geopolitical dynamics impact the industry, the Bangor airport has continued to see growth
and has experienced a moderate to small impact on operation.
Airport Director Saavedra discussed an emergency runway closure due to Alkali-Silica
Reaction that required major repair and provided an unbudgeted expense.
Airport Director Saavedra shared that the connector project is expected to be completed
in mid-October. He provided updates on projects Taxiway Alpha and Mike as well as the
TSA Checkpoint expansion.
Chair Leonard expressed support for the growth approaches.
Councilor Carson asked whether the expansion includes brining outside businesses into
the space -- Airport Director Saavedra responded no, the TSA Checkpoint expansion is
limited to the screening area. 
Councilor Beck commended the progress with Taxiway Alpha and Mike.
Airport Director Saavedra discussed new proposed terms of the GE Vernova temporary
land lease. 
Councilor Carson moved that the Committee recommend the lease change to full Council
for approval. Seconded by Councilor Fish. Roll call vote conducted – all in favor, none
opposed. Motion passed.
Airport Director Saavedra discussed the recommendation to accept and appropriate the
Airport Improvement Grant.
Councilor Carson moved staff recommendation to accept and appropriate the Airport
Improvement Grant payment. Seconded by Councilor Faloon. Roll call vote conducted –
all in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.
3. Electric Vehicles and Heat Pumps Follow-Up
Chair Leonard introduced the agenda item.
Planning Officer Collette provided follow-up responses to Councilor Fish’s questions from
a previous presentation about electric vehicles, discussing battery longevity, insurance
costs, and fuel sources of the energy grid.
Planning Officer Collette discussed heating efficiency, cost of cooling, and the value of
heat pumps. She expressed that heat pump efficiency can be informed by evaluating how
it is being used.
Councilor Fish and Councilor Carson thanked her for the response and additional
information.
Chair Leonard expressed appreciation for opening up a larger dialogue surrounding
energy use and efficiency in the city. 
Planning Officer Collette discussed the exploration of grant opportunities to help support
the cost to install solar. Councilor Carson asked about what infrastructure upgrades may
be needed. Councilor Fish discussed the option of town-owned electric companies.
Councilor Carson shared an experience with a city-owned power company.
4. Potential Chicken Regulations Follow-Up
Chair Leonard introduced the agenda item.
Planning Officer Collette discussed previously presented regulations and the feedback to
look into other options, such as to reference the City of Auburn’s regulations
Planning Officer Collette recommended allowing up to four hens on lots 0.49 acres or less
and up to 12 on lots 0.5 acres or larger, prorated on actual lot size. She discussed
proposed coop setbacks along with the requirement to receive a Certificate of Occupancy
for coops to ensure Code Enforcement and Animal Control can evaluate compliance.
Councilor Carson asked whether issues with rodent prevention measures within a coop
could constitute as evidence relating to increased rodent presence. 
Councilor Beck asked about the enforceability process. Planning Officer Collette
discussed that the timeline will depend on Code Enforcement, and that once staff receives
a report, they go to inspect the complaint. Beck asked whether the recommendations
would go to a public hearing – Collette responded it will be included in the Land
Development Code updates and associated public hearings.
Councilor Deane expressed concern surrounding what occurs if the chickens are not being
well taken care of. Planning Officer Collette discussed uncertainty of how to regulate care
levels, and shared staff will explore potential provisions further. 
Councilor Carson discussed the additional workload that the Code Enforcement team may
incur. Councilor Beck asked about the ability to deputize the inspections.
5. Executive Session: Consultations with legal counsel 1 M.R.S.A § 405(6)(E)
Councilor Carson moved that pursuant to 1 M.R.S.A § 405(6)(E), consultations with legal
counsel, the Committee enter Executive Session. Seconded by Councilor Faloon. Roll
call vote conducted – all in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.
6. Possible Actions on Executive Session Item
Chair Leonard discussed the end of the current moratorium on data centers expiring in
October. He asked the Committee whether the moratorium should be continued to provide
staff more time to develop potential regulations.
Councilor Fish discussed that she is in favor of extending the moratorium, but would like
to weigh the legal risk of challenges associated with the moratorium. She expressed
interest in strict ordinances that would discourage data centers while limiting legal risk for
the city.
Councilor Carson asked for an estimate with time required to continue developing a
regulatory framework – Planning Officer Collette discussed that potentially within six
months, and noted the priority of public engagement in forming regulations. 
Councilor Carson moved that the Committee recommends extending the data center
moratorium for six months to full Council. Seconded by Councilor Fish. Vote unless
doubted, no doubt. 
Meeting adjourned at 7:45 P.M.
Meeting minutes respectfully submitted,
Kayleigh Rienas
Development Assistant
Community & Economic Development Department
